diagram_math_checks.evidence: The left panel has one braid strand and is labelled e in B_1. Each other panel has exactly two strands and one half twist, labelled e sigma_1 or e sigma_1^{-1} in B_2. For n=1, the existing stabilization definition gives iota_1(e) sigma_1^{+/-1}; no extra factor or generator occurs.

Geometric time increases upward. In the positive panel, the strand from bottom position 1 to top position 2 is broken from (0.54,1.08) to (0.66,1.32); the strand from bottom 2 to top 1 is continuous. This projects the elementary positive half twist with the left starting point below the disk midpoint and the positive second disk coordinate toward the viewer, as required by the local half-twist supplier and F1.

In the negative panel the bottom-2 to top-1 strand has the underpass gap from (0.66,1.08) to (0.54,1.32), while the bottom-1 to top-2 strand is continuous. Thus only over/under data reverse; strand permutation and upward orientations do not reverse.

Every outer return arc joins the top endpoint at a horizontal position to the bottom endpoint at that same position, with downward arrows compatible with upward strand arrows. No return arcs intersect one another or the braid strands except their endpoints. The identity gives one cycle; both signed crossings give permutation (1 2), and following bottom 1 -> top 2 -> bottom 2 -> top 1 -> bottom 1 gives one closed component, as F3 and verification step 1.1 require.

Each stabilized planar closure has a single crossing and empty lobes, so one signed oriented R1 move removes the crossing and yields a planar circle, matching verification step 2.1 and F2. The prose explicitly treats these as schematic oriented-link diagrams and invokes no arbitrary change of the fixed closure framing and no isotopy fixing the axis. No framed-link equivalence is claimed.
The entire original Example, Facts and three Verification steps are byte-identical and precede the added Remarks. Their proof does not refer to the new figure.
